bc_woodbury_bluffs.blurb: Woodbury Bluffs is a cliff on the slope above Kootenay Lake, near Woodbury Creek north of Nelson. The wall stretches several hundred metres across and stands roughly 40 to 70 metres tall, with rock that is clean for this part of the Kootenays. Most lines are short sport climbs of about half a pitch, with a handful of two or three pitch routes and some mixed ground. Eight of the nine routes here are bolted and one is trad. Grades cluster around 5.10 and 5.11, with one 5.12 and a single 5.13 for the strong.

bc_h_the_octagon.blurb: The Octagon is a small boulder sector within the Grand Wall Boulders, at the foot of the Stawamus Chief above Squamish. It takes in the Octagon boulder itself plus the problems just to its east, nine in all. Most of them sit between V0 and V3, with one around V5 and a single V8 for strong climbers. The wider Grand Wall boulder forest is shaded and cool, though landings across it can be uneven because of rocks and roots, so a few smaller pads are useful.
bc_h_the_octagon.approach: Take the second Psych Ledge trail, the Superfly and Grand Wall trail that starts at a BC Parks sign, past the Superfly boulder to a junction; the Octagon boulder is just to the right.
